data.name: Mallik
data.gender_notes: Mallik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mallik is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘mallika’ which means 'lord of wealth'. In Hindu mythology, Mallik is an alternate name for Vishnu or Krishna, who is known to bestow wealth and prosperity upon his devotees. The name Mallik carries the meaning “God of wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mallik usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mallik total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Mallik is a popular Hindu name, predominantly found in the Indian subcontinent. It is a name that symbolizes wealth, prosperity, and abundance. In Indian culture, giving a child a name with the 'Mallik' prefix is believed to bless the child with vast and rich experiences throughout his/her life. This name is often chosen for individuals from prosperous or affluent families, and is considered auspicious and meaningful.
data.spiritual_significance: Mallik holds deep spiritual significance, as it is associated with the divine names of Vishnu and Krishna. In Hinduism, Vishnu is known as the preserver of the universe, and is believed to be the source of all wealth and prosperity. Krishna, on the other hand, is the embodiment of divine love and assurance, and is often described as the giver of boons. By adopting the name Mallik, one seeks the blessings of these divine beings, and embodies the qualities of wealth, prosperity, and love in their life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mallik is a Sanskrit name meaning 'Lord of All'. It is a title of reverence for Krishna, symbolizing his supreme authority over all creation. It is also a name for Shiva, representing his omnipotent and all-encompassing nature.
